title: Start Screen Redesign: Rotating Demo, Expand Panels, Footer
content:
## Overview

The main menu (start screen) was redesigned around three changes: an animated isometric snake demo as a hero visual, inline expandable panels for bot-mode selection (replacing always-visible dropdowns), and a low-prominence footer for the leaderboards and GitHub links.

## Rotating snake demo

- **`src/menu-demo.ts`** implements a `MenuDemo` class: a fully self-contained, animated snake simulation rendered on a dedicated `<canvas id="menu-demo-canvas">` embedded in the menu's `.menu-hero` section.
- It is intentionally independent of the main game renderer/`SnakeGame` state machine — it has its own game state, its own `requestAnimationFrame` loop, and its own isometric projection code (ground plane, checkerboard tiles, grid lines, perspective-scaled blocks with top/side faces, block shadows). This keeps its lifecycle (start/stop/restart) decoupled from an active game session, so it can't interfere with real gameplay and is safe to run purely for visual effect.
- The demo drives its snake using the **same configurable bot used in actual gameplay** rather than a scripted path, so the animation always looks competent and dynamic and automatically improves alongside future bot changes.
- The camera continuously rotates around the isometric board, giving motion and immediately communicating the game's 3D aesthetic without requiring interaction. The projection math (including perspective strength and a per-frame coordinate cache for performance) mirrors the main game's isometric renderer. On snake death the demo pauses briefly then restarts.
- The canvas edges are faded into the background using a **CSS radial-gradient mask** (in `src/style.css`) rather than drawing a fade inside the canvas itself. This keeps rendering code free of presentation concerns and avoids a visible rectangular frame around the animation; the title/tagline text is layered over the canvas as an overlay.
- `src/main.ts` instantiates `MenuDemo` on startup and calls `start()`/`stop()` in sync with screen transitions: the demo runs only while the menu screen is shown and stops whenever any other screen is displayed, avoiding wasted off-screen animation work.

## Expandable bot-selection panels

- Bot selectors for "Solo Bot" and "Bot vs Bot" modes are no longer shown as always-visible dropdowns on the menu. Instead, `index.html` defines an expand-control per mode: clicking the mode's button hides that trigger button and reveals an inline panel (`.expand-panel`) containing the bot picker(s), a description, and Cancel/Launch actions.
- The panel expands in place rather than opening a modal or navigating to a separate screen, keeping the interaction lightweight, reversible, and free of an overlay layer.
- The trigger button is hidden while its panel is open (rather than shown in a toggled/active state), which avoids the layout growing tall with both button and panel visible and makes the panel's Cancel button the obvious way back.
- `src/main.ts` provides `setExpandPanel` and `closeAllExpandPanels` helpers to manage this show/hide toggle. Cancel collapses the panel; Launch closes the panel first, then starts the game. Returning to the menu from any screen closes all open panels.
- `setupBotSelectors` targets the panel-scoped select elements — `bvb-bot1-select`, `bvb-bot2-select`, `demo-bot-select` — the old top-level menu selector elements were removed entirely.
- `src/style.css` defines `.expand-control`, `.expand-panel`, `.expand-panel-row`, and `.expand-panel-actions`, including a short fade-in animation on open. `.menu-buttons` is a vertical column layout with a constrained max-width.

## Footer with leaderboards and GitHub links

- The leaderboards button was demoted out of the primary button stack into a new `.menu-footer` bar at the bottom of the menu, reflecting its lower priority relative to starting a game.
- A GitHub link (pointing to the repository) was added alongside it, separated by a decorative dot.
- Both links share a `.footer-link` style in `src/style.css` that strips standard button chrome, uses muted text color, and only highlights (green) on hover — without the scale/background hover transforms used on regular buttons. This keeps primary call-to-action buttons visually dominant while preserving the leaderboards feature and adding project navigation.

## Files involved

- `src/menu-demo.ts` — new `MenuDemo` class (self-contained demo simulation/renderer)
- `src/main.ts` — demo start/stop wiring, expand-panel helpers, bot selector targeting
- `index.html` — `.menu-hero` canvas placement, expand-control/panel markup, `.menu-footer` markup
- `src/style.css` — canvas edge mask, expand-panel styles, footer-link styles, `.menu-buttons` layout
